value.name: writer denies outside influence
value.description: The speaker insists that neither Rosa nor Lucia influenced the decision being described.
evidence: Rosa does not know I have done this. Lucia does not know I have done this. I have not told either of them because I did not want them to feel they had to defend a decision that is mine alone.

value.name: mother addresses Daniel with affection
value.description: The speaker directly tells Daniel she loves him and has always loved him before making a difficult declaration.
evidence: Daniel — mi hijo, mi primero — I love you. I have always loved you.
You have wanted this house since you were sixteen years old.

value.name: speaker rejects Daniel's claim to the house
value.description: The speaker explains that Daniel wants the house for status and recognition, but denies that he truly held the family together.
evidence: You have wanted this house since you were sixteen years old. You wanted it then because you thought it would make you the head of something. You want it now because you think it will repay you for the years you have spent feeling that you were the one who held us together.
Hijo, you did not hold us together. Rosa did. I did. Your sister did, in her way, from far away, by being a person we could be proud of.

You held yourself together, which is a different and harder thing, and I am proud of you for it, but it is not the same thing as holding the family, and I will not pretend it is, not even now, not even to spare you.

value.name: speaker grants Lucia a share of the house
value.description: The speaker tells Lucia that the house belongs to her in thirds and that she may stay or leave freely.
evidence: Lucia — you have wanted to come home for a long time and have not known how.
The house is yours, in thirds, and Rosa will not put you out, and your brother, if he is the man I believe he can still become, will not either.
Stay if you want to stay. Go if you want to go.

value.name: speaker frames house as nonpunitive
value.description: The speaker clarifies that the house is not meant as punishment, implying a final decision about its meaning or inheritance.
evidence: The house is not a punishment and it is
